title: Training Note on the Estimate Hold in Credit Balance Refunds
content:
**The rule.** On the Employer Unemployment Insurance Tax Accounts, an estimate hold scales what is left of a credit balance refund once every other amount has been taken off: two or more estimated assessments booked on the account within the estimate hold months, 6, leave nothing to refund; exactly one scales it by 0.5; none leaves it whole. The refund is rounded to the cent once, after this scaling.

| Estimated assessments booked within 6 months | What is left is multiplied by |
|---|---|
| Two or more | 0 — nothing to refund |
| Exactly one | 0.5 |
| None | 1 — left whole |

The 6 months are counted in whole months back from the day of the request, by the entry dates of the estimated assessments in the account's balance history. Only contribution assessments that rest on an estimate count.

## Questions and answers (hypothetical amount left of USD 419.26)

**One estimated assessment booked 4 months before the request?** 419.26 multiplied by 0.5 is **USD 209.63**.

**Two estimated assessments, booked 2 and 5 months before?** Nothing is left to refund: **USD 0.00**.

**One booked 4 months before and one 8 months before?** Only the first lies within the 6 months, so the amount is scaled by 0.5: **USD 209.63**.

**None within the 6 months?** The amount is left whole: **USD 419.26**.
